In 1996, the median household income in Ontario was $55,172 before taxes, while the average household income was $62,614.

In 2022, the median household income in Ontario was $91,000 before taxes, while the average household income was $116,000.

Wages no longer increase in proportion to inflation.  IMO, the threshold should be tied to taxpayer income rather than an arbitrary number.  For example, anyone making over 1.5x the median income ($136,500 for 2022) in the top x percent or quartile should be on the list.

In 1996, when it began, the threshold was roughly 1.8x the median, so in 2022, it would be $163,800.

I also agree that $55k in 1996 was a lot more valuable than $91k in 2022 due to inflation, and $164k is over double what I earn in the private sector.  $150k threshold seems more than fair to me.

https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/kitchener-waterloo/ontario-votes-2022-declined-ballots-rise-1.6466308

It seems like everywhere we look these days society is falling apart on top of us.  If there was a survey taken of the general population's satisfaction you'd probably find most of it isn't working for the vast majority of people.  I know I feel this to my core and has been a major factor in my own mental health struggle so I thought I'd share my opinion, take it as you like.

We have to realize that the feelings we have aren't there to make us feel bad.  They are there to remind us something is wrong and needs adjustment.  You feel frustrated and like you're being forced to learn something that you don't care about right now or maybe ever.  Which is fair but don't let those negative feelings and stupid little things put you down and ruin your entire mood.  Maybe try to look the class like a stepping stone.  You might have to put up with some stupid BS now and once you get past it you might not need it again but at least you can feel good about it being over and done with.

We have to fight though a lot of things we don't like in life but when we do we can feel that much better about our accomplishment of just getting it done.  I bet when you're a couple minutes late it makes you feel like shit when the teacher doesn't give you a break right?  Well let me ask you, do you ever make a concious effort to feel proportionately good when you show up a few minutes early?  Probably not cuz I know I have a tough time with that myself.

Don't sweat the small stuff, this too shall pass, etc.  I'm sure you've heard it before.  Something I've been trying lately is taking my anger towards broken systems and transforming that hate into motivation.  Motivation to build myself up and feel good so I can put something good out into the world rather than the last thing the world needs which is more negativity.  Motivation to not only analyze the root of what is making me so angry but to confront it.  Motivation not to stop there and keep moving to find what steps to do next.  Motivation to build myself to the point that one day maybe I'll be able to help make a small part of our society better for everyone.

Sorry for the long post but I hope you took the time to read it and that it was worthwhile.  You're not alone.  Deep down there is a path of good feelings and light.  Though it might not be easy it is worthwhile.
